=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1093]] is assessed at 58% (possible). Glasgow protocols identify an elder John’s son John in 1563 and again a younger John in 1570–71. The generation fits the Hirmanscheillis testator of 1577, whose death excludes both the elder John (dead by June 1575) and Ninian’s brother John (alive in 1613). This makes the documented son a useful preferred candidate for the rural testator.

The father–son wording is explicit for the burgh Johns; identifying that son with the Hirmanscheillis husband of Margaret Hoghame remains a possible inference, without an estate or residence bridge.

Next useful test: Compare protocol property names with Hirmanscheillis testament associates and land transfers.

Source basis already held: [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n52/mode/2up Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 3, protocol 748, 13 May 1563, scan (https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n52/mode/2up); vol. 6, protocol 1722, 8 January 1570/71, scan (https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc05scogoog/page/n58/mode/2up).]; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills National Records of Scotland, John Glasgow testament dative, CC8/8/5 images 276-277: John Glasgow]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
